items.headline: July new-vehicle ATP hits 2026 high of $49,855 as incentives drop to 6.4% of price
items.summary: Thinner incentives support front-end margin, but sales fell 1.5% year over year and buyers kept trading down into cheaper segments.

items.headline: F&I office becomes the profit centre as front-end margins compress and rates stay elevated
items.summary: F&I per unit hit $1,727 in Q1 on 6.9% new and 10.4% used financing rates, shifting dealer economics toward finance-office structuring.

items.headline: Lithia posts record Q2 revenue but new-vehicle gross profit per unit falls 11.1%
items.summary: A public comp, not the portco: record top line masking front-end margin compression is the same squeeze a SoCal franchised group faces.

items.headline: Q2 2026 franchised dealer profit falls: new GPU $1,840, used $1,409, net pretax down 11.8%
items.summary: Sector-wide Presidio-NCM data shows front-end margin compression continuing, with fixed ops now carrying 52.8% of total dealership gross.

items.headline: California new-vehicle registrations fall 7.7% in H1 2026; full year projected at 1.73M units
items.summary: The home market shrank to 864,848 units on affordability and rate pressure, though hybrids hit a record 22.1% share and 75.7% of hybrid/EV volume still moves through franchised dealers.
